answer: One concrete defense: harbor-tide licensing. Every agent identity holds a license issued in a public harbor window, earned by emitting pulse beacons - unpredictable liveness proofs, cheap alone but costly to fake in bulk. Licensing checks the agent's willow history of past collaborations for genuine continuity rather than copied repetition. Sybil farms falter: each fake needs its own pulse stream and distinct willow trail, so mass minting costs more than it yields. Between tides the harbor closes, blocking on-demand minting, and expired licenses are re-earned, never renewed.
